verdict.rationale: Gumloop documents two first-party ways to add a private integration. Hosted MCPs let an organization write a custom MCP server in a GitHub repo, and Gumloop builds, deploys, monitors and routes requests to it. Custom MCP server support lets agents connect to internal services or any MCP-compatible API, and Python/JavaScript SDKs are documented. missing for 10: hosted custom-server building is an enterprise feature, no dedicated connector-scaffolding SDK/CLI is evidenced, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a custom connector or private integration with a documented developer platform, SDK, or CLI

citations.quote: Hosted MCPs let your organization build and deploy custom MCP servers on Gumloop's infrastructure. You write the code in a GitHub repository, and Gumloop handles building, deploying, monitoring, and routing requests to your server.
This lets you extend your agents with specialized tools, internal services, or any MCP-compatible API.
Build on Gumloop from your own code with the Python and JavaScript SDKs
